title: Corey Haines's launch playbook: SLC readiness gate, ORB channels, five-phase rollout
summary: An open-source launch skill Corey wrote for AI agents. It argues for launching repeatedly, not once. It gates launches on a Simple, Lovable, Complete product. It structures marketing across owned, rented and borrowed channels, rolls out in five phases, and sizes announcements to the size of each update.

principles.text: Launch again and again; every feature and update is a chance to capture attention.
principles.quote: The best companies don't just launch once—they launch again and again. Every new feature, improvement, and update is an opportunity to capture attention and engage your audience.

principles.text: Funnel all launch traffic from rented and borrowed channels into owned channels.
principles.quote: Structure your launch marketing across three channel types. Everything should ultimately lead back to owned channels.

principles.text: Rented channels give speed, not stability; pull momentum into your owned ecosystem.
principles.quote: Rented channels give speed, not stability. Capture momentum by bringing users into your owned ecosystem.

principles.text: Borrowed audiences only pay off if you convert that attention into owned relationships.
principles.quote: Borrowed channels give instant credibility, but only work if you convert borrowed attention into owned relationships.

principles.text: Ship an SLC v1: one thing, lovable, and complete. Avoid both stealth mode and endless feature adding.
principles.quote: Cut scope until one thing is lovable and complete, then launch that. SLC gives you a real launch now instead of a perfect launch never.

principles.text: Scale marketing effort to update size; use changelogs for minor updates and full campaigns for major ones.
principles.quote: Even small changelog updates remind customers your product is evolving. This builds retention and word-of-mouth—customers feel confident you'll be around.
